Kingship of Christ
KING-ship uhv KRYST
doctrinal phrase
From king and Christ; the doctrine of Christ’s kingly office, one of His three mediatorial offices.

📖 Biblical Definition

The kingship of Christ is the doctrine of His kingly office, one of the three offices—prophet, priest, and king—by which He executes His work as Mediator. As King, Christ reigns over all things by right of His deity and by the Father’s appointment of the Mediator: all power in heaven and earth is given unto Him, and He must reign till He hath put all enemies under His feet. His kingship is exercised in three spheres. He rules His church by His Word and Spirit, gathering, governing, and defending His people, the sole Head and Lawgiver of His church, so that the conscience is bound by His commands alone. He rules providentially over the whole created order and the nations, governing history for the good of His church and the glory of God. And He will rule openly and visibly at His return, when every knee shall bow and He shall judge the world in righteousness. His kingdom is not of this world in origin or weapons—it comes not by sword or political conquest but by the gospel and the Spirit—yet it lays claim to every sphere, for there is no neutral ground over which the King does not reign. The dictionary holds the kingship of Christ as the comfort of His people and the claim upon all men: the crucified Servant is the crowned King, His reign is now and not yet, and the certain end of history is the universal acknowledgment of His Lordship.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Christ’s kingly office, one of His three mediatorial offices; He reigns over His church by Word and Spirit, over providence and the nations, and will reign openly at His return.

KINGSHIP OF CHRIST, His kingly office as Mediator.

One of the three offices—prophet, priest, and king—of His mediatorial work.

All power in heaven and earth given unto Him; He must reign till all enemies are subdued.

He rules His church by Word and Spirit as its sole Head and Lawgiver.

He rules providence and the nations, and will reign openly at His return.

📖 Key Scripture

Mat 28:18 — "And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth."

1Co 15:25 — "For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet."

Joh 18:36 — "Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence."

Rev 19:16 — "And he hath on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Christ’s kingship is either reduced to inward sentiment or distorted into a political program won by worldly power.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the present, real, and comprehensive reign of Christ, exercised by His Word and Spirit and not by carnal weapons. His kingdom is not of this world in its origin and means—it does not advance by the sword or by seizing the levers of political power—yet it is no mere inward feeling; it lays claim to every sphere and will be openly vindicated at His return. The error on one side privatizes His reign into a sentiment in the heart.

The error on the other side would make His kingdom a worldly political program won by force, confusing the church’s spiritual weapons with the magistrate’s sword. The dictionary keeps the balance the Scripture sets: Christ reigns now over all things for His church, He governs the conscience by His Word alone, He overrules the nations in providence, and He will return to reign visibly. His Lordship is total but His weapons are the gospel and the Spirit; the King who refused the crowd’s crown and the tempter’s kingdoms now reigns, and shall reign, King of kings and Lord of lords.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The doctrine sets forth Christ’s threefold reign—over His church, over providence, and in His coming glory.

expand to see more

Greek basileus — king; basileia — kingdom, reign, rule.

The threefold office: prophet, priest, and king, the munus triplex.

Christ reigns by right of deity and by the Father’s appointment of the Mediator.

His church-rule is by Word and Spirit; His sole headship binds the conscience.

“King of kings and Lord of lords” names His supreme and final dominion.

Usage

"The kingship of Christ is taught as one of His three mediatorial offices."

"His sole headship over the church is cited against binding the conscience by human laws."

"“My kingdom is not of this world” guards against both privatizing and politicizing His reign."
